stem: Assuming enough trauma team members are available, which one of the following could immediately become a parallel priority in this case?

options.text: Notifying Brayden’s parents of the incident
Alerting theatres of a likely emergency case

explanation: In trauma care, pain relief can be commenced in parallel with the primary survey when adequate staff are available and the patient remains under close monitoring. Severe pain from a suspected limb fracture should be treated promptly without delaying essential trauma assessment.

citations.title: Practice Quiz: Emergency Medicine - Trauma 2 - Pain

rationale: The key concept is that pain management should not be delayed while the trauma primary survey is underway, provided sufficient personnel are present to maintain safety and monitoring.

optionExplanations.A: Not an immediate clinical priority in trauma management.
optionExplanations.B: Important communication, but not a parallel emergency priority during initial trauma care.
optionExplanations.C: Correct: analgesia can be given early in parallel with the primary survey when staffing allows.
optionExplanations.D: May become relevant if operative management is likely, but not the immediate parallel priority asked here.
optionExplanations.E: Not relevant to emergency trauma management.

Clinical scenario 1 - Braydon

The following six questions refer to Brayden’s clinical scenario.

Teaching/learning points:

Pain relief

Primary survey in context of distracting injury

Paramedics arrive in the emergency department with Brayden, a 12 year old boy. They were called to attend after Brayden lost control of his quadbike (recreational vehicles) while riding around in a field. He was found on his back, alert and screaming in pain. Eyewitnesses stated he had been travelling at approximately 40kph when he lost control at a bend and the quadbike rolled.

Brayden has an obvious deformity to his right lower limb. He was wearing a helmet, which was removed at the scene. He is transported to ED on a spinal board with hard collar in situ. Vital signs are Resp rate 28/min, Sats 100% in air, Heart rate 100bpm, BP 118/65. He has a grossly deformed right leg, with a firm, swollen thigh and he is screaming in pain.
